verses.1: While they were conversing and wishing for an auspicious victory, the night quickly passed for the great-souled Shatrughna.
verses.2: Then, in that clear morning, the brave demon, impelled by his hunger for food, came out of the city.
verses.3: In the meantime, the brave Shatrughna, having crossed the Yamuna river, stood at the gate of Madhupura with his bow in hand.
verses.4: Then, as midday arrived, that cruel demon came, carrying the burden of many thousands of living beings.
verses.5: Then he saw Shatrughna standing at the gate, holding a weapon, and the demon then asked him, "What will you do with this?"
verses.6: "O vilest of men, I have devoured thousands of armed individuals like you out of anger; do you indeed desire death?"
verses.7: The demon, addressing Shatrughna, exclaims that Shatrughna, the vilest and evil-minded of men, has today entered his mouth by himself, thus becoming his complete meal.
verses.8: As the demon spoke thus and laughed repeatedly, the valiant Shatrughna shed tears out of intense anger.
verses.9: From the great-souled Shatrughna, who was overcome by such rage, radiant rays of light emanated from all his limbs.
verses.10: And Shatrughna, greatly enraged, spoke to that demon, declaring his wish to engage in single combat with the evil-minded one.
verses.11: I am Shatrughna, the son of Dasharatha and brother of the wise Rama, the eternal slayer of enemies, and I have come here desiring your death.
verses.12: Grant me, who desires battle, a single combat, for you are an enemy to all beings, and you shall not escape me alive.
verses.13: As he spoke thus, the demon, as if laughing, replied to the best of men, "Fortunately, O evil-minded one, you have arrived!"
verses.14: O foolish one, O lowest of men, my maternal uncle Ravana, the lord of demons, was killed by Rama for the sake of a woman.
verses.15: I tolerated all that, the destruction of Ravana's lineage, but I have especially shown contempt towards you all from the very beginning.
verses.16: Indeed, all of them, past, present, and future, including you, O lowest of men, have been killed and insulted by me as if they were mere grass.
verses.17: O evil-minded one, I will give you the battle you desire; just wait for a moment until I bring and prepare the kind of weapon you wish for.
verses.18: Shatrughna quickly said to him, "Where will you go alive from me? An enemy, once seen by chance, should not be released by a resolute person."
verses.19: Indeed, whoever gives an advantage to an enemy with a wavering mind is killed due to his dull-wittedness, just like a coward.
verses.20: Therefore, take a good look at the world of the living, for I shall lead you, a sinful enemy of the three worlds and of Rama, towards Yama's abode with various sharp arrows. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 68 ।। Thus ends the sixty-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
